aa241.q: A patient with atrial fibrillation has depressed cardiac function. Which listed drug should be avoided?
opts: Digoxin is listed to slow the ventricular rate in atrial fibrillation; depressed cardiac function is on the avoid list for verapamil.
Amiodarone's listed dangers are lung, thyroid, eye, skin and liver toxicity; depressed cardiac function is on the avoid list for verapamil.
Dofetilide is listed for normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation, with torsades as its danger; depressed cardiac function is on verapamil's avoid list.
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem are to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias, sick sinus syndrome and depressed cardiac function; they are negative inotropes.

aa241.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Which arrhythmias are a listed indication for propranolol?
opts: Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate; propranolol is listed for supraventricular arrhythmias.
Correct. Propranolol is listed for supraventricular arrhythmias, ventricular ectopic beats and myocardial infarction.
Recurrent ventricular tachycardia resistant to other drugs is an amiodarone (class III) indication; propranolol is listed for supraventricular arrhythmias.
Life-threatening sustained ventricular arrhythmias are a flecainide (class IC) indication; propranolol is listed for supraventricular arrhythmias.

aa241.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Which two antiarrhythmic classes flatten phase 4 in the slow-response pacemaker cells of the nodes?
opts: Correct. Beta blockers (class II) and calcium channel blockers (class IV) share the same picture: a flatter phase 4 in pacemaker cells, so the next beat comes later.
Classes IA and IC slow phase 0 in fast-response working cells; the classes that flatten phase 4 in pacemaker cells are II and IV.
Class IB shortens and class III prolongs phase 3; the classes that flatten phase 4 in pacemaker cells are II and IV.
Classes I and III act on the working-cell action potential (phase 0 and phase 3); classes II and IV flatten phase 4 in pacemaker cells.

aa241.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Which effects does propranolol have on the heart?
opts: Propranolol lowers contractility as well as rate; both its inotropic and chronotropic effects are negative.
Propranolol slows the heart rate as well as lowering contractility; both effects are negative.
Correct. Propranolol has negative inotropic and chronotropic effects, slows atrioventricular conduction and reduces phase 4 activation.
Both of propranolol's effects are negative: it lowers contractility and slows the rate.

aa241.q: In which rhythms should verapamil and diltiazem be avoided?
opts: Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem are to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias, sick sinus syndrome and depressed cardiac function.
Atrial fibrillation is a listed indication for verapamil and diltiazem, not a reason to avoid them.
Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia is the first listed indication for verapamil and diltiazem, not a reason to avoid them.
Atrial flutter is an atrial rhythm like the listed atrial fibrillation; the arrhythmias in which to avoid verapamil and diltiazem are ventricular.

aa241.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Which antiarrhythmic class is made up of the beta receptor antagonists?
opts: Class I drugs are the sodium channel blockers (IA, IB, IC); the beta receptor antagonists are class II.
Correct. Class 2 antiarrhythmics are the beta receptor antagonists, such as propranolol, metoprolol, acebutolol and esmolol.
Class III drugs prolong repolarization through potassium; the beta receptor antagonists are class II.
Class IV drugs are the calcium channel blockers verapamil and diltiazem; the beta receptor antagonists are class II.

aa241.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Which beta blocker is the intravenous, short-acting one?
opts: Propranolol is the nonselective beta blocker used as the class II example; the intravenous short-acting one is esmolol.
Correct. Esmolol is the intravenous, short-acting beta blocker.
Metoprolol is a beta-1 selective blocker with less bronchospasm; the intravenous short-acting one is esmolol.
Sotalol is a beta blocker that also inhibits potassium channels; the intravenous short-acting beta blocker is esmolol.

aa241.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: A patient with asthma needs a beta blocker for a supraventricular arrhythmia. Which is preferred?
opts: Propranolol is nonselective and bronchospasm is on its toxicity list, so it is the one to avoid in asthma.
ruled out by a stated finding
Sotalol has beta-blocking activity with bronchospasm on its toxicity list, and it adds potassium channel block; metoprolol causes less bronchospasm.
ruled out by a stated finding
Propafenone's beta-blocking activity brings bronchospasm, and it is a class IC drug; metoprolol is beta-1 selective with less bronchospasm.
ruled out by a stated finding
Correct. Metoprolol is beta-1 selective and causes less bronchospasm than propranolol, which matters in asthma.

aa241.q: Why are class IV calcium channel blockers avoided in depressed cardiac function?
opts: Correct. Class IV drugs are negative inotropes, so verapamil and diltiazem are to be avoided in depressed cardiac function.
Class IV drugs lower contractility rather than raising it; that negative inotropic effect is why depressed function is on their avoid list.
Marked QT prolongation is listed for dofetilide; class IV drugs are avoided in depressed function because they are negative inotropes.
Sodium channel block is the class I mechanism; class IV drugs block L-type calcium channels and are negative inotropes.

aa241.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Why are verapamil and diltiazem used with caution in liver damage?
opts: They are eliminated unchanged by the kidneys
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys is dofetilide's; verapamil and diltiazem are metabolized in the liver.
Hepatic dysfunction is an adverse effect of amiodarone; verapamil and diltiazem need caution because the liver metabolizes them.
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem undergo hepatic metabolism, so caution is advised in liver damage.
Loading doses are for amiodarone, with its 40-day half-life; verapamil and diltiazem need caution because of hepatic metabolism.

aa241.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Verapamil and diltiazem belong to which antiarrhythmic class?
opts: Class I drugs are sodium channel blockers; verapamil and diltiazem are class IV calcium channel blockers.
Class II drugs are beta blockers, which act on the same nodes; verapamil and diltiazem are class IV calcium channel blockers.
Class III drugs prolong repolarization through potassium; verapamil and diltiazem are class IV.
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem are the class IV calcium channel blockers; they block the L-type channel and slow atrioventricular node conduction.

aa241.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa241.q: Besides arrhythmias, which cardiac condition is a listed indication for propranolol?
opts: Heart failure is on propranolol's toxicity list (it is a negative inotrope), not its indication list.
Heart block is a toxicity of propranolol, from slowed atrioventricular conduction, not an indication.
Correct. Propranolol's indications are supraventricular arrhythmias, ventricular ectopic beats and myocardial infarction.
Sick sinus syndrome is a reason to avoid verapamil and diltiazem; propranolol's listed cardiac indication is myocardial infarction.

aa242.q: Which condition can a beta-1 selective blocker such as metoprolol still worsen?
opts: Thrombocytopenia is listed for quinidine and flecainide; metoprolol and acebutolol can still worsen congestive heart failure.
Glaucoma contraindicates disopyramide because of its anticholinergic action; metoprolol can still worsen congestive heart failure.
Seizures are a contraindication to lidocaine; metoprolol can still worsen congestive heart failure.
Correct. Metoprolol and acebutolol cause less bronchospasm, but congestive heart failure remains on their list.

aa242.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Why is propranolol a concern in a patient with asthma?
opts: Pneumonitis, with pulmonary fibrosis, is amiodarone's lung toxicity; propranolol's concern in asthma is bronchospasm.
Respiratory paralysis is listed for magnesium sulfate; propranolol's concern in asthma is bronchospasm.
Pulmonary fibrosis (potentially fatal) belongs to amiodarone; propranolol's concern in asthma is bronchospasm.
Correct. Propranolol is nonselective, and bronchospasm is on its toxicity list; a beta-1 selective blocker causes less.

aa242.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Which channel do class IV antiarrhythmics block?
opts: Correct. Class IV drugs block the L-type calcium channel, decrease automaticity, slow atrioventricular node conduction and are negative inotropes.
The fast sodium channel is blocked by class I drugs; class IV blocks the L-type calcium channel.
Reducing potassium efflux is the class III mechanism; class IV blocks the L-type calcium channel.
The sodium-potassium ATPase is inhibited by digoxin; class IV blocks the L-type calcium channel.

aa242.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Where are verapamil and diltiazem most effective?
opts: Greatest effect in ischemic tissue is the class IB (lidocaine) feature; verapamil and diltiazem work best in the most active tissue.
Affecting the normal heart is a class IC feature; verapamil and diltiazem are most effective in the most active tissue.
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem block both activated and inactivated channels and are most effective in the most active tissue.
Verapamil and diltiazem block activated and inactivated channels, so they work best in the most active tissue, not resting tissue.

aa242.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Class II antiarrhythmics slow the heart mainly by which effect on pacemaker cells?
opts: Correct. Class II drugs decrease phase 4 depolarization, so pacemaker cells reach threshold later; they also slow conduction and prolong atrioventricular conduction.
Slowing the phase 0 upstroke is the class I sodium channel blocker effect; class II flattens phase 4 in pacemaker cells.
Prolonging phase 3 is the class III potassium channel blocker effect; class II decreases phase 4 depolarization.
Shortening phase 3 is the class IB (lidocaine) effect; class II decreases phase 4 depolarization.

aa242.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Metoprolol and acebutolol are which type of beta blocker?
opts: Nonselective describes propranolol, which carries more bronchospasm; metoprolol and acebutolol are beta-1 selective.
Correct. Metoprolol and acebutolol are beta-1 selective blockers, similar to propranolol but with less bronchospasm.
Beta blockers that block potassium channels
A beta blocker that also inhibits potassium channels is sotalol (class II plus class III); metoprolol and acebutolol are beta-1 selective.
Beta blockers that block sodium channels
Sodium channel block with beta-blocking activity describes propafenone (class IC); metoprolol and acebutolol are beta-1 selective.

aa242.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Which of these beta blockers is nonselective?
opts: Metoprolol is a beta-1 selective blocker with less bronchospasm; propranolol is the nonselective one.
Acebutolol is a beta-1 selective blocker like metoprolol; propranolol is the nonselective one.
Correct. Propranolol is a nonselective beta blocker, which is why it carries the bronchospasm risk.
Esmolol is the intravenous, short-acting beta blocker; the nonselective beta blocker here is propranolol.

aa242.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Which arrhythmia is a listed indication for verapamil and diltiazem?
opts: Verapamil and diltiazem are to be avoided in ventricular arrhythmias; their indications are paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia and atrial fibrillation.
Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate; verapamil and diltiazem are listed for supraventricular tachycardia and atrial fibrillation.
Ventricular fibrillation is a ventricular arrhythmia, where verapamil and diltiazem are to be avoided; their indications are supraventricular.
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem are listed for supraventricular tachycardia (paroxysmal) and atrial fibrillation.

aa242.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Which adverse effects are expected with verapamil and diltiazem?
opts: Bronchospasm belongs to propranolol and fatigue to metoprolol and acebutolol; verapamil and diltiazem cause hypotension and edema.
Correct. Hypotension and edema are the listed toxicities of verapamil and diltiazem.
Flushing, shortness of breath and chest burning are adenosine's; verapamil and diltiazem cause hypotension and edema.
Nystagmus and seizures belong to lidocaine's central nervous system toxicity; verapamil and diltiazem cause hypotension and edema.

aa242.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Which central nervous system effects are listed for metoprolol and acebutolol?
opts: Seizures and nystagmus are part of lidocaine's central nervous system toxicity; metoprolol and acebutolol cause sedation and fatigue.
Correct. Central nervous system sedation and fatigue are listed for metoprolol and acebutolol, with congestive heart failure.
Tinnitus and blurred vision, with dizziness, are quinidine's cinchonism; metoprolol and acebutolol cause sedation and fatigue.
Neuropathy, muscle weakness and ataxia belong to amiodarone; metoprolol and acebutolol cause sedation and fatigue.

aa242.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: Which conduction disorder is a listed toxicity of propranolol?
opts: Correct. Propranolol slows atrioventricular conduction, and heart block is on its toxicity list with heart failure and hypotension.
Propranolol has a negative chronotropic effect, so it slows rather than speeds the rate; its listed conduction toxicity is heart block.
Marked QT prolongation is listed for dofetilide, a potassium channel blocker; the conduction toxicity listed for propranolol is heart block.
Torsades de pointes belongs to class IA, dofetilide and sotalol; propranolol's listed conduction toxicity is heart block.

aa242.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa242.q: What do verapamil and diltiazem do to the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes?
opts: Speed both the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes
Speeding conduction is the reverse of their action; verapamil and diltiazem suppress the sinoatrial node and decrease atrioventricular conduction.
Hyperpolarize both nodes through potassium channels
Hyperpolarizing cells through atrial potassium channels is adenosine; verapamil and diltiazem block calcium channels.
Suppress the sinoatrial node, slow the atrioventricular node
Correct. Verapamil and diltiazem suppress the sinoatrial node and decrease atrioventricular conduction.
Shortening phase 3 is the class IB effect in working muscle; verapamil and diltiazem suppress the sinoatrial node and slow atrioventricular conduction.
